hypotheses.title: Vinblastine Sulfate Extends Lifespan Through Gut Stem Cell Microtubule Inhibition
hypotheses.claim: Vinblastine Sulfate extends lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster by inhibiting microtubule polymerization in gut stem cells. This mechanism slows intestinal stem cell proliferation and preserves gut homeostasis during ageing.
hypotheses.rationale: Microtubule polymerization drives the proliferative activity of gut stem cells, and unchecked intestinal turnover contributes to tissue degeneration. Suppressing this process can maintain barrier integrity and reduce age-related gut dysfunction.
hypotheses.prediction: Treated flies will live longer than controls and show reduced gut stem cell division and improved intestinal integrity.
hypotheses.experiment: Administer Vinblastine Sulfate to adult Drosophila melanogaster and measure lifespan alongside gut stem cell proliferation and microtubule polymerization markers, using a microtubule-resistant rescue group to confirm mechanism.

hypotheses.title: Dihydrorotenone Extends Lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster
hypotheses.claim: Dihydrorotenone extends lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster. Supplementation with this compound increases median and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Mild modulation of mitochondrial electron transport can induce adaptive stress responses that enhance cellular resilience. Such hormetic effects are a recognized route to slower ageing and extended survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Dihydrorotenone-treated flies will show significantly greater median and maximum lifespan than vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Compare lifespan cohorts of Drosophila melanogaster fed Dihydrorotenone against vehicle controls across multiple doses under identical conditions.

hypotheses.title: Royal Jelly Shortens Lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster
hypotheses.claim: Royal Jelly shortens lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster. Flies receiving Royal Jelly supplementation exhibit reduced median and maximum lifespan compared with controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Royal Jelly contains potent growth-stimulating factors that can activate nutrient-sensing and reproductive pathways. Chronic activation of these pathways often accelerates ageing and reduces survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Royal Jelly-fed flies will show significantly shorter median and maximum lifespan than vehicle-fed controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Raise matched cohorts of Drosophila melanogaster on diets with and without Royal Jelly and compare survival curves under identical housing and density conditions.

hypotheses.title: Royal Jelly Extends Lifespan by Activating Insulin/IGF Signalling
hypotheses.claim: Royal Jelly extends lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster by activating the insulin/IGF signalling pathway. This activation triggers downstream metabolic programmes that improve somatic maintenance and survival.
hypotheses.rationale: Insulin/IGF signalling regulates nutrient storage, stress resistance and tissue renewal. Controlled activation of this pathway can coordinate metabolic adaptation that supports longevity.
hypotheses.prediction: Royal Jelly-fed flies will live longer than controls and show elevated insulin/IGF pathway activity, while pathway-deficient mutants will not gain lifespan.
hypotheses.experiment: Feed Royal Jelly to Drosophila melanogaster and to insulin/IGF signalling mutants, comparing lifespan and pathway activity readouts between all groups.
